title: Memory management and garbage collection
summary: The Common Language Runtime (CLR) owns the managed heap: generations, the Small Object Heap (SOH), Large Object Heap (LOH), and Pinned Object Heap (POH), roots, mark-and-compact, ArrayPool and MemoryPool, pinning and weak references, and a finalizer thread you should almost never rely on. Learn workstation versus server garbage collection, DATAS, Dispose versus finalizers (including SkiaSharp), allocation traps, container tuning, and how that differs from V8.

topics.title: Stack versus heap layout (where values and objects live)
Generations, Small Object Heap, and Large Object Heap (SOH and LOH)
Roots, mark, and compact (how the GC finds live objects)
Garbage collection modes in microservices (server, workstation, containers)
V8 garbage collection versus CLR garbage collection (comparison)
ArrayPool and MemoryPool (reuse buffers without LOH churn)
Pinned Object Heap and weak references (interop and caches)
